غزل‌های جامی

Reviewed ghazals · close translations, occurrence-specific word analysis, grammar notes, and verb breakdowns

غزل شمارهٔ 1

O you whose beauty appears in all that appears: may a thousand holy souls be sacrificed for you.

Moment by moment I lament separation from you like the reed—stranger still, I am not apart from you for a single breath.

It is love alone that manifests itself in both worlds, now in a king’s robes and now in a beggar’s garb.

One sound reaches your ear in two forms: sometimes you call it ‘summons,’ and sometimes ‘echo.’

Rise, cupbearer, and graciously pour a draught for the grief-stricken lovers from that grief-dispelling cup.

When that special cup delivers me from selfhood, nothing but God remains in the eye of direct vision.

Jami, there is no road of guidance to God except love. We have spoken—and peace be upon whoever follows guidance.

غزل شمارهٔ 2

The name of our beloved is a talisman protecting souls. How mighty is His name, and how exalted!

His name is the treasure-map of the divine realm: through it the hidden treasure of the unseen is revealed.

All the divine names are manifestations of the Essence; all things are manifestations of the names.

I see nothing in existence except Him: the name of ‘other’ and the image of ‘other-than-Him’ have been effaced.

There is absolute being and pure unity. Where is “he”? Where are “you” and “I”?

I, he, and you vanished from between us; the mystery of unity became uniquely one, beyond all multiplicity.

Jami’s soul cannot endure separation from the subtle truth of unity, as a fish cannot endure separation from the sea.
